intro: Cape Neddick is a village in the town of York on the southern coast of Maine, known for its lighthouse on the Nubble. Inland, at the edge of the woods beside Cape Neddick Road, a reader found a broad old oak whose twisting limbs spread over the road, and sent us its photograph with three words: very old and very big.

trees.story:
"Very old and very big!" wrote the reader who sent us this oak from Cape Neddick, on the southern coast of Maine, and the photograph bears out both.

It stands at the edge of the woods beside Cape Neddick Road, far wider than anything around it. A short, dark trunk splits low down into several great limbs that lean out in every direction, twisting and doubling back as they climb, and the crown they carry spreads over the road on one side and the gravel verge on the other. Behind it the younger trees of the wood stand straight and thin, which makes the old oak look broader still. In the reader's November picture the crown holds a last scatter of brown leaves against a clear blue sky.

Oaks usually grow this wide and low only in open ground, so it may once have stood in a field or at a pasture edge before the woods closed in, but we do not know its history. We do not know its species for certain either, or its girth; tell us here if you do.

See it from the verge, and mind the traffic.
